findings.title: T-02 early session_id capture persists across resume-fallback, causing postWork to resume the wrong session in grace-exit path
findings.rationale: extractedSessionId is declared at run() scope and never reset between runQuery calls. T-02 captures OLD_SESSION_ID from call 1's init message. If call 1 fails and resume-fallback triggers call 2 (fresh session), the T-02 guard `if (!extractedSessionId)` blocks capture of the new session's id. If call 2 grace-exits (no success result), extractedSessionId remains OLD_SESSION_ID. postWork prompts execute with `resume: OLD_SESSION_ID`, applying rules follow-up to the wrong (stale) session context. Applies to: fixer steps (resumeSessionId set) + resume failure + grace fires in fallback session + postWorkPrompts configured. Pre-T-02 behavior was safe: call 1 failure left extractedSessionId undefined, and call 2's success result provided the correct id. T-02 introduced this regression by not resetting extractedSessionId at the resume-fallback boundary.

findings.title: D5 outer catch fires during follow-up phases, returning stale followUpAttempts=0 / addedTurns=ZERO when turns were already consumed
findings.rationale: The outer catch covers the entire try block: main work turn + report retry + postWork + output repair. D5 condition (`abortController.signal.aborted && capturedToolResult !== null`) triggers for hard abort in ANY of these phases. If abort fires during postWork after one postWork turn already completed (postWork++), D5 returns `followUpAttempts: 0` and `addedTurns: ADDED_TURNS_ZERO` — both stale/inaccurate. The numeric invariant `reportRetry + outputRepair === followUpAttempts` holds (0+0=0), but the semantic invariant (counts reflect actual turns consumed) breaks. Design intent (design.md D5) describes D5 as a backup for pre-grace hard aborts, not for follow-up phase aborts. Options: (A) Accept as-is — D5 is a rare backup path and metrics inaccuracy in an already-degraded scenario is acceptable. (B) Narrow D5 catch scope to cover only main work turn, and handle follow-up phase abort separately.

options.label: Accept as-is (A)
options.consequence: followUpAttempts/addedTurns are inaccurate when abort fires during postWork. Usage telemetry undercounts consumed turns. Rare scenario, no correctness impact.

options.label: Narrow D5 scope or track partial counts (B)
options.consequence: Requires restructuring the catch boundary or tracking follow-up counts outside the try block. Higher implementation complexity but accurate metrics.

findings.title: D5 path omits touchedFiles from AgentRunResult, discarding touchedFileMessages collected during main work turn
findings.rationale: D5 return object does not include `touchedFiles`. `touchedFileMessages` is populated during the main work turn (assistant messages) but `extractTouchedFilesFromMessages` is not called in D5 path. CommitOrchestrator interprets `touchedFiles: undefined` as 'this runtime does not record touched files' and skips the entry. The D3 grace-exit path (happy path) correctly propagates touchedFiles. The pre-existing timeout path also omits touchedFiles, so the regression increment is small. Fix: call `extractTouchedFilesFromMessages(touchedFileMessages, cwd)` in D5 path and include it in the return object.

findings.title: D5 path calls sessionLogWriter.close() without calling writeSummary(), leaving session log without summary entry
findings.rationale: The happy path calls `sessionLogWriter.writeSummary({ sessionId, model, modelUsage })` then `sessionLogWriter.close()`. D5 path calls only `sessionLogWriter?.close()`. Session log file is missing the summary line (session id, model, token usage) when D5 fires. The pre-existing timeout path has the same omission, so this is not a new regression pattern. Functional impact: debug log incomplete. Fix: call `sessionLogWriter?.writeSummary({ sessionId: extractedSessionId, model: resolvedConfig.model, modelUsage: extractedModelUsage })` before `close()` in D5 path.

observations.title: Grace-exit from inner catch correctly propagates through outer try/finally
observations.rationale: The `return { lastResult }` from inside the inner catch propagates through the outer try/finally (which only does clearTimeout + removeEventListener + armReportGrace=null). No exceptional path from finally cleanup. The return correctly exits runQuery and continues through the happy path for postWork, result file read, and success settle.

observations.title: settledByReport vs shared abort check is race-safe in single-threaded JS
observations.rationale: The check `settledByReport && !abortController.signal.aborted` is atomic in single-threaded JS event loop. No interleaving between the two conditions is possible. The grace timer and shared abort are separate macrotasks; whichever fires first determines the path.

observations.title: mainQueryOptions spread correctly overrides shared abortController with mainQueryAbort
observations.rationale: `{ ...queryOptions, abortController: mainQueryAbort }` puts mainQueryAbort last, correctly overriding `queryOptions.abortController` (shared). postWork and output-repair spread `queryOptions` directly without override, so they use the shared controller as intended.
